status_summary: HHS and USDA issued the 2025-2030 Dietary Guidelines in January 2026; the guidelines are signed by both Secretaries, and the bill status and text of H.R. 8578 give the issue date as 2026-01-07. The guidelines document runs about ten pages, prioritizes protein, recommends full-fat dairy without added sugar, advises sharply limiting highly processed foods and added sugar, and does not mention environmental sustainability, which matches the chapter's minimum reform option of keeping the guidelines focused on nutrition. The supplemental Scientific Foundation report states that the agencies chose not to adopt the 2025 advisory committee report as the basis and instead relied on reviews compiled by an NIH researcher with NIH-coordinated external peer review, while still scoring each advisory committee recommendation as implemented or not. H.R. 8578, the FRESH Act, introduced 2026-04-29 and referred to the House Agriculture Committee with no later action, would bar modifying the 2025-2030 edition except as the statute allows and make future editions take effect only if approved by Congress by law; no repeal bill was found. On 2026-08-19 the Physicians Committee for Responsible Medicine sued HHS and USDA in the US District Court for the District of Columbia under the Federal Advisory Committee Act (one news report also cites the Administrative Procedure Act), seeking withdrawal of the guidelines; no ruling was found.

timeline.event: HHS and USDA announce the Dietary Guidelines for Americans, 2025-2030 (White House briefing dated 2026-01-07 per the program website); the guidelines are signed by the HHS and USDA Secretaries.

The guidelines document is published: a roughly ten-page text that prioritizes protein and whole foods, recommends full-fat dairy without added sugar, and advises limiting highly processed foods and added sugar; it does not discuss environmental sustainability.

The supplemental Scientific Foundation report and appendices are posted (the appendices file name carries the date 1.28.26; the report states the 2025 advisory committee report was not used as the basis).

H.R. 8578, the FRESH Act, was introduced and referred to the House Committee on Agriculture; its text would bar modifying the 2025-2030 guidelines except as the statute allows and make future editions take effect only if approved by Congress by law.

The Physicians Committee for Responsible Medicine filed suit against USDA and HHS in the US District Court for the District of Columbia, alleging violations of the Federal Advisory Committee Act in the process used for the 2025-2030 Dietary Guidelines and seeking their withdrawal; no ruling was reported.
